types.embedding_query_text: Person: A human individual with a distinct identity Also called Individual, Celebrity, Artist, PublicFigure, Member. Examples: Sophia Laforteza, Manon Bannerman, Laforteza, Sophia.

chosen_type.label: Person
chosen_type.justification: Schema.org's Person class directly matches the definition and mentions as individual human beings.

candidates.label: Person
candidates.comment: A Person is an individual human being, whether alive, dead, undead, or fictional. Also called individual, human, character. Examples: John Doe, Albert Einstein, Sherlock Holmes. Distinct from Organization, which is a group of people.

candidates.label: IndividualProduct
candidates.comment: An IndividualProduct is a single, identifiable instance of a product. Also called specific product unit, unique item, serialized product. Examples: a laptop with a specific serial number, a particular copy of a book, a unique piece of art. Distinct from ProductModel, which describes a class of products, and ProductGroup, which is a collection of products.

candidates.label: MemberProgramTier
candidates.comment: An intangible representing a specific tier within a loyalty or membership program. Also called membership level, loyalty tier, program status. Examples: "Gold Member", "Platinum Tier", "Basic Membership Level".

candidates.label: Organization
candidates.comment: An Organization is a group of people with a particular purpose, such as a school, NGO, corporation, or club. Also called entity, institution, association. Examples: Google, Harvard University, Red Cross, a local sports club. Distinct from Person, which is an individual.

candidates.label: Taxon
candidates.comment: A cohesive biological unit representing a group of organisms, such as a species, genus, or family. Also called biological classification, taxonomic group, species, genus. Examples: Homo sapiens, Canis familiaris, Felidae (cat family), Plantae (plant kingdom).

types.embedding_query_text: MusicGroup: A collective of musicians performing together Also called Band, Ensemble, GirlGroup, PopGroup, Group. Examples: Katseye, the ensemble, the group.

chosen_type.label: MusicGroup
chosen_type.justification: Schema.org's MusicGroup aligns with the definition of a collective of musicians and the example 'Katseye'.

candidates.label: MusicGroup
candidates.comment: A MusicGroup, as a PerformingGroup, is an organization of musicians, such as a band or orchestra, or a solo musician. Also called band, musical ensemble, orchestra, solo artist. Examples: The Beatles, New York Philharmonic, Taylor Swift. Distinct from PerformingGroup, which is a broader category for any performance group.

candidates.label: PerformingGroup
candidates.comment: A PerformingGroup is an organization of performers, such as a band, orchestra, or circus. Also called performance ensemble, troupe, artistic group. Examples: Cirque du Soleil, a local theatre company, a dance troupe. Distinct from MusicGroup, which is specifically for musical performers.

candidates.label: DanceGroup
candidates.comment: A DanceGroup is a performing organization specializing in dance, often presenting choreographed performances. Also called dance company, ballet troupe, dance ensemble, dance collective. Examples: Alvin Ailey American Dance Theater, Riverdance, New York City Ballet, Bolshoi Ballet.

candidates.label: TheaterGroup
candidates.comment: An organization or company dedicated to producing and performing theatrical works. Also called theater company, drama troupe, acting ensemble. Examples: The Royal Shakespeare Company, Cirque du Soleil, a local amateur dramatics society.

candidates.label: MusicEvent
candidates.comment: A MusicEvent is an event primarily featuring musical performances. Also called concert, musical performance, gig. Examples: a rock concert, a classical symphony performance, a music festival. Distinct from PerformingArtsEvent, which includes broader performance types like theatre or dance.

types.embedding_query_text: RecordLabel: A company that manages and promotes musical artists Also called MusicLabel, EntertainmentCompany, Label, ManagementCompany, Agency. Examples: HYBE x Geffen Records, the label.

chosen_type.label: MusicLabel
chosen_type.definition: A company that manages and promotes musical artists
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class for a record label exists; 'MusicLabel' is a subclass of Organization.

candidates.label: MusicAlbum
candidates.comment: A MusicAlbum, as a MusicPlaylist, is a collection of music tracks released together. Also called album, record album, studio album. Examples: 'Thriller' by Michael Jackson, 'Abbey Road' by The Beatles, a compilation album. Distinct from MusicRecording, which is usually a single song.

candidates.label: MusicAlbumReleaseType
candidates.comment: MusicAlbumReleaseType is an enumeration describing the kind of release for a music album. Also called release format, album release category. Examples: Single, EP, Album. Distinct from MusicAlbumProductionType, which describes the content type.

candidates.label: MusicRelease
candidates.comment: A MusicRelease, as a MusicPlaylist, is a specific release of a music album, often with particular formats or editions. Also called album release, record release, music edition. Examples: a vinyl release of an album, a digital download version, a deluxe edition CD. Distinct from MusicAlbum, which is the conceptual collection of tracks.

candidates.label: MusicReleaseFormatType
candidates.comment: MusicReleaseFormatType is an enumeration describing the format of a music release. Also called release media type, recording format. Examples: CDFormat, DigitalAudioRecording, VinylFormat, CassetteFormat. Distinct from MusicAlbumReleaseType, which describes the kind of release (e.g., single, EP).

candidates.label: MusicAlbumProductionType
candidates.comment: MusicAlbumProductionType is an enumeration classifying a music album by its content type. Also called album type, production category. Examples: StudioAlbum, LiveAlbum, Soundtrack, CompilationAlbum. Distinct from MusicAlbumReleaseType, which describes the release format.

types.embedding_query_text: Song: A musical composition performed by an artist Also called Track, Composition, Single, Hit, Music. Examples: Gnarly, Pinky Up, Gabriela.

chosen_type.label: MusicComposition
chosen_type.justification: Schema.org's MusicComposition matches the definition of a musical composition and the song examples.

candidates.label: MusicRecording
candidates.comment: A MusicRecording, as a CreativeWork, is a recorded performance of a musical composition, usually a single song. Also called music track, song recording, audio track. Examples: 'Yesterday' by The Beatles (the recorded version), a single from an album, a demo track. Distinct from MusicComposition, which is the abstract musical work.

candidates.label: MusicComposition
candidates.comment: A MusicComposition is a musical work, such as a song or symphony, that can be performed or recorded. Also called musical piece, song, score. Examples: Beethoven's 5th Symphony, 'Bohemian Rhapsody' by Queen, a jingle. Distinct from MusicRecording, which is a recorded performance of a composition.

candidates.label: MusicAlbum
candidates.comment: A MusicAlbum, as a MusicPlaylist, is a collection of music tracks released together. Also called album, record album, studio album. Examples: 'Thriller' by Michael Jackson, 'Abbey Road' by The Beatles, a compilation album. Distinct from MusicRecording, which is usually a single song.

candidates.label: MusicPlaylist
candidates.comment: A MusicPlaylist, as a CreativeWork, is an ordered collection of music tracks. Also called playlist, music compilation, track list. Examples: a Spotify playlist, a radio station's daily playlist, a custom mix CD. Distinct from MusicAlbum, which is a formally released collection of tracks.

candidates.label: SheetMusic
candidates.comment: Printed or written musical notation, as distinct from a performance or recording. Also called musical score, notation, music manuscript, song sheet. Examples: a piano concerto score, guitar tablature, a vocal sheet for a song, an orchestral score.

types.embedding_query_text: Event: A scheduled or recurring activity with a defined purpose Also called Award, Ceremony, Performance, Announcement, Occasion. Examples: Grammy Awards.

chosen_type.label: MusicEvent
chosen_type.justification: Schema.org's MusicEvent fits the Grammy Awards as a music-focused event.

candidates.label: Event
candidates.comment: An Event is a Thing happening at a specific time and location, such as a concert, lecture, or festival. Also called happening, occurrence, occasion. Examples: A rock concert, a public lecture, a sports match, a community festival.

candidates.label: MusicEvent
candidates.comment: A MusicEvent is an event primarily featuring musical performances. Also called concert, musical performance, gig. Examples: a rock concert, a classical symphony performance, a music festival. Distinct from PerformingArtsEvent, which includes broader performance types like theatre or dance.

candidates.label: ConferenceEvent
candidates.comment: An event specifically organized as a conference, typically involving presentations, discussions, and networking. Also called conference, convention, symposium, summit. Examples: A tech conference, an academic symposium, a business summit, a medical convention. Distinct from Event, which is a general occurrence.

candidates.label: SportsEvent
candidates.comment: An event involving athletic competition or display. Also called athletic contest, game, match, sporting competition. Examples: a football game, an Olympic event, a marathon race, a tennis tournament.

candidates.label: EducationEvent
candidates.comment: An EducationEvent is an Event focused on learning or instruction. Also called educational activity, learning event, training session. Examples: A university lecture, a workshop on coding, a seminar on financial literacy, a school field trip.

types.embedding_query_text: Date: A specific calendar date Also called Day, CalendarDate, TimeReference, TemporalPoint, DayOfYear. Examples: 2023, September, February.

chosen_type.label: Date
chosen_type.definition: A calendar date without time component, representing a temporal marker for events.
chosen_type.justification: Schema.org's Date data type aligns with the mentions of calendar dates like '2023' and 'September'.

candidates.label: Date
candidates.comment: Date is a data type representing a specific calendar date, typically formatted according to ISO 8601. Also called calendar date, specific day. Examples: "2023-10-27", "1999-12-31", "0001-01-01".

candidates.label: DayOfWeek
candidates.comment: An enumeration representing a specific day of the week, used for scheduling or recurring events. Also called Weekday, calendar day, day name. Examples: Monday, Tuesday, Saturday, Sunday. Distinct from Date, which specifies a particular calendar date.

candidates.label: DateTime
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, combining both date and time components according to ISO 8601. Also called Timestamp, date and time string, ISO 8601 datetime. Examples: "2023-10-27T10:30:00Z", "1999-12-31T23:59:59-05:00", "2024-01-15T14:00:00". Distinct from Date, which only specifies a calendar date without time.

candidates.label: Time
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, typically in hh:mm:ss format, potentially with a timezone offset. Also called timestamp, clock time, time of day. Examples: "14:30:00", "09:00:00Z", "17:45:30+01:00".

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

types.embedding_query_text: FanBase: A community of supporters for a particular artist or group Also called Supporters, Audience, Followers, Fans, FanCommunity. Examples: EYEKONS.

chosen_type.label: Audience
chosen_type.justification: Schema.org's Audience class represents a community of supporters, fitting the 'EYEKONS' example.

candidates.label: Audience
candidates.comment: An Audience is an Intangible entity representing the specific group of people for whom an item or creative work is intended. Also called target group, readership, viewership, demographic. Examples: children, teenagers, medical professionals, general public, investors.

candidates.label: UserPlusOnes
candidates.comment: An outdated type representing a user's interaction of giving a "+1" endorsement, typically on Google+ or similar platforms. Also called user endorsement, +1, social recommendation. Examples: a user giving a +1 to a web page, endorsing a business, recommending content.

candidates.label: PeopleAudience
candidates.comment: A PeopleAudience, as an Audience, describes a set of characteristics belonging to people, e.g., who compose an item's target audience. Also called demographic group, target audience, human audience. Examples: 'adults aged 18-35', 'students', 'retirees'. Distinct from Audience, which is a broader category including non-human audiences.

candidates.label: MedicalAudience
candidates.comment: An audience type representing target groups for medical web pages. Also called healthcare audience, patient demographic, medical readership. Examples: "patients", "healthcare professionals", "medical researchers", "general public interested in health".

candidates.label: MemberProgramTier
candidates.comment: An intangible representing a specific tier within a loyalty or membership program. Also called membership level, loyalty tier, program status. Examples: "Gold Member", "Platinum Tier", "Basic Membership Level".

types.embedding_query_text: Duration: A length of time between two points Also called Period, TimeSpan, Interval, Length, Term. Examples: 23-year-old, six months.

chosen_type.label: Duration
chosen_type.justification: Schema.org's Duration fits the 'six months' example as a time span, though '23-year-old' is ambiguous.

candidates.label: Duration
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Duration represents a period of time, typically expressed in ISO 8601 format. Also called time span, period, length of time. Examples: "PT1H30M" (1 hour 30 minutes), "P3D" (3 days), "PT2H" (2 hours).

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

candidates.label: ServicePeriod
candidates.comment: A structured value representing a duration for a service, often including constraints like cutoff times or business days. Also called service duration, operational window, delivery timeframe, handling period. Examples: a 2-day shipping period with a 3 PM cutoff, a 5-business-day processing time, a 24/7 support period.

candidates.label: Time
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, typically in hh:mm:ss format, potentially with a timezone offset. Also called timestamp, clock time, time of day. Examples: "14:30:00", "09:00:00Z", "17:45:30+01:00".

candidates.label: DateTime
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, combining both date and time components according to ISO 8601. Also called Timestamp, date and time string, ISO 8601 datetime. Examples: "2023-10-27T10:30:00Z", "1999-12-31T23:59:59-05:00", "2024-01-15T14:00:00". Distinct from Date, which only specifies a calendar date without time.

types.embedding_query_text: Threat: A hostile or menacing statement directed at an individual or group Also called Intimidation, Harassment, Menace, Danger, ThreateningBehavior. Examples: online death threats.

chosen_type.label: Message
chosen_type.justification: Schema.org's Message class represents hostile statements like 'online death threats'.

candidates.label: Conversation
candidates.comment: A series of one or more messages exchanged between individuals or organizations on a specific topic. Also called discussion, dialogue, chat, discourse. Examples: An email thread, a text message exchange, a forum discussion, a spoken dialogue. Distinct from Comment, which is a single remark on an item.

candidates.label: DisagreeAction
candidates.comment: A react action expressing a negative opinion or difference of opinion regarding an object, proposition, or theme. Also called Express disagreement, object to, dispute, dissent. Examples: Disagreeing with a political statement, objecting to a proposed plan, disputing a fact. Distinct from AgreeAction, which expresses positive sentiment or agreement.

candidates.label: UserComments
candidates.comment: An outdated type representing a user's interaction of posting comments or feedback. Also called user comment, public comment, feedback post. Examples: a user leaving a comment on a blog post, posting a review, providing feedback on a product.

candidates.label: DislikeAction
candidates.comment: A react action expressing a negative sentiment or disapproval towards an object, proposition, or theme. Also called Express dislike, disapprove of, show aversion, downvote. Examples: Disliking a movie, expressing disapproval of a policy, downvoting a comment online. Distinct from LikeAction, which expresses positive sentiment or approval.

candidates.label: Message
candidates.comment: A creative work representing a single communication from a sender to one or more recipients. Also called communication, dispatch, note, email. Examples: an email, a text message, a direct message on social media, a voicemail.

chosen_type.label: GroupMemberCount
chosen_type.definition: A numerical count of members in a group
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class exists for member counts; 'GroupMemberCount' is a subclass of Thing.

candidates.label: MemberProgram
candidates.comment: An intangible loyalty or membership program that offers specific benefits to its members. Also called loyalty program, membership scheme, rewards program. Examples: an airline frequent flyer program, a supermarket loyalty card, a gym membership.

candidates.label: MemberProgramTier
candidates.comment: An intangible representing a specific tier within a loyalty or membership program. Also called membership level, loyalty tier, program status. Examples: "Gold Member", "Platinum Tier", "Basic Membership Level".

candidates.label: WearableSizeGroupEnumeration
candidates.comment: An enumeration of common size groups or types for wearable products. Also called apparel size group, clothing size type, garment category. Examples: "men's", "women's", "children's", "unisex".

candidates.label: DENonprofitType
candidates.comment: DENonprofitType is an enumeration representing specific types of non-profit organizations recognized under German fiscal code, article 52. Also called German non-profit classification, AO 52 non-profit. Examples: A German charitable foundation, a registered German association for public benefit.

candidates.label: SizeGroupEnumeration
candidates.comment: An enumeration of common size groups used for various product categories. Also called size category, apparel size group, product size range. Examples: 'Adult', 'Kids', 'Petite', 'Plus Size'.
